title: SiGNoR: Similarity-based Graph Partitioning and Node Reuse for Memory Efficient GNN Acceleration
problem: GNNs require large memory, and graph partitioning for on-chip memory creates halo nodes that lead to frequent redundant external DRAM access.
motivation: Edge and mobile applications demand memory-efficient GNN deployment but memory constraints limit scalability.
method: Hardware-friendly graph partitioning with similarity-based node reuse replacing halo nodes with local nodes, multiphase partitioning for boundary refinement, and partition-wise block floating-point for energy efficiency.
key_novelty: Similarity-based node replacement strategy reducing redundant halo node DRAM access by leveraging local partition nodes.
limitations: Tested on specific graph datasets; generalization to other graph structures may vary.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient GNN acceleration via similarity-based partitioning
